import sys
import tracemalloc
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

SCRIPTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "skills/brotli-checker/scripts"
sys.path.insert(0, str(SCRIPTS))
import brotli_dependencies as dependencies  # noqa: E402


def test_requirement_sampling_does_not_split_the_entire_input_into_lines():
    text = "brotli\r\n" * 200000
    tracemalloc.start()
    try:
        rows = dependencies.dependency_matches(text, "requirements.txt")
        _, peak = tracemalloc.get_traced_memory()
    finally:
        tracemalloc.stop()
    assert len(rows) == dependencies.DEPENDENCY_MATCH_LOOKAHEAD
    assert rows[-1] == {"line": 21, "text": "brotli"}
    assert peak < len(text)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("name", "text", "expected"),
    [
        (
            "setup.py",
            (
                'from setuptools import setup\nrequirements = ["brotlicffi"]\n'
                'setup(description="Brotli benchmark", install_requires=requirements)'
            ),
            ["brotlicffi"],
        ),
        (
            "setup.cfg",
            (
                "[metadata]\ndescription = Brotli benchmark\n[options]\n"
                "install_requires =\n  brotli>=1.2.1\n"
            ),
            ["brotli>=1.2.1"],
        ),
        (
            "pipfile",
            '[scripts]\nbenchmark = "brotli --help"\n[packages]\nbrotli = "*"\n',
            ['"*"'],
        ),
        (
            "pipfile.lock",
            (
                '{"_meta":{"description":"Brotli benchmark"},'
                '"default":{"brotlicffi":{"version":"==1.2.1.0"}}}'
            ),
            ['{"version": "==1.2.1.0"}'],
        ),
        (
            "app.csproj",
            (
                "<Project><PropertyGroup><Description>Brotli benchmark</Description>"
                '</PropertyGroup><ItemGroup><PackageReference Include="BrotliSharpLib" '
                'Version="0.3.3" /></ItemGroup></Project>'
            ),
            ["BrotliSharpLib"],
        ),
        (
            "Directory.Packages.props",
            (
                '<Project xmlns="urn:test"><ItemGroup>'
                '<PackageVersion Include="BrotliSharpLib" Version="0.3.3" />'
                "</ItemGroup></Project>"
            ),
            ["BrotliSharpLib"],
        ),
        (
            "app.nuspec",
            (
                '<package><metadata><dependencies><dependency id="BrotliSharpLib" />'
                "</dependencies></metadata></package>"
            ),
            ["BrotliSharpLib"],
        ),
        (
            "packages.config",
            '<packages><package id="BrotliSharpLib" version="0.3.3" /></packages>',
            ["BrotliSharpLib"],
        ),
        (
            "packages.lock.json",
            '{"dependencies":{"net9.0":{"BrotliSharpLib":{"resolved":"0.3.3"}}}}',
            ["BrotliSharpLib"],
        ),
        (
            "app.deps.json",
            (
                '{"libraries":{"BrotliSharpLib/0.3.3":{}},'
                '"targets":{".NETCoreApp":{"BrotliSharpLib/0.3.3":{}}}}'
            ),
            ["BrotliSharpLib/0.3.3", "BrotliSharpLib/0.3.3"],
        ),
    ],
)
def test_python_and_dotnet_dependencies_are_extracted_from_owned_fields(name, text, expected):
    assert [match["text"] for match in dependencies.dependency_matches(text, name)] == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("name", "text"),
    [
        ("setup.py", 'setup(description="Brotli benchmark", install_requires=["zlib"])'),
        ("setup.cfg", "[metadata]\ndescription = Brotli benchmark\n[options]\nzip_safe=true"),
        ("pipfile", '[scripts]\nbenchmark = "brotli --help"\n[packages]\nzlib = "*"'),
        ("pipfile.lock", '{"_meta":{"description":"Brotli benchmark"},"default":{}}'),
        ("requirements.txt", "# Install Brotli for an optional benchmark\n-r brotli.in\nzlib"),
        (
            "app.csproj",
            (
                "<Project><PropertyGroup><Description>Brotli benchmark</Description>"
                '</PropertyGroup><ItemGroup><None Include="brotli-results.txt" />'
                "</ItemGroup></Project>"
            ),
        ),
        (
            "app.nuspec",
            "<package><metadata><description>Brotli benchmark</description></metadata></package>",
        ),
        (
            "packages.lock.json",
            '{"description":"Brotli benchmark","dependencies":{"net9.0":{"zlib":{}}}}',
        ),
        (
            "app.deps.json",
            '{"description":"Brotli benchmark","libraries":{"zlib/1.0":{}}}',
        ),
    ],
)
def test_descriptions_scripts_comments_and_nonpackage_items_are_not_dependencies(name, text):
    assert dependencies.dependency_matches(text, name) == []


def test_dotnet_xml_comments_and_cdata_are_not_package_items():
    text = """<Project>
<!-- <PackageReference Include="BrotliSharpLib" /> -->
<![CDATA[<PackageReference Include="BrotliSharpLib" />]]>
<ItemGroup><PackageReference Include="zlib" /></ItemGroup>
</Project>
"""
    assert dependencies.dependency_matches(text, "app.csproj") == []


def test_requirements_support_named_extras_vcs_editable_and_direct_urls():
    text = """# Brotli prose is ignored.
httpx[brotli]>=0.28
git+https://example.invalid/project.git#egg=brotlicffi
-e git+https://example.invalid/project.git#egg=Brotli
https://example.invalid/releases/brotli-1.2.1.tar.gz
--extra-index-url https://brotli.example.invalid/simple
"""
    assert dependencies.dependency_matches(text, "requirements-dev.txt") == [
        {"line": 2, "text": "httpx[brotli]>=0.28"},
        {"line": 3, "text": "git+https://example.invalid/project.git#egg=brotlicffi"},
        {"line": 4, "text": "-e git+https://example.invalid/project.git#egg=Brotli"},
        {"line": 5, "text": "https://example.invalid/releases/brotli-1.2.1.tar.gz"},
    ]


def test_requirements_support_local_renamed_direct_and_editable_equals_sources():
    text = """./vendor/brotli
codec @ git+https://github.com/google/brotli
--editable=git+https://example.invalid/project.git#egg=brotlicffi
codec@git+https://github.com/google/brotli
vendor/brotlicffi
C:\\vendor\\brotli
../ordinary-zlib
"""
    assert dependencies.dependency_matches(text, "requirements.txt") == [
        {"line": 1, "text": "./vendor/brotli"},
        {"line": 2, "text": "codec @ git+https://github.com/google/brotli"},
        {
            "line": 3,
            "text": "--editable=git+https://example.invalid/project.git#egg=brotlicffi",
        },
        {"line": 4, "text": "codec@git+https://github.com/google/brotli"},
        {"line": 5, "text": "vendor/brotlicffi"},
        {"line": 6, "text": "C:\\vendor\\brotli"},
    ]


def test_setup_literals_do_not_follow_calls_or_extra_names_as_dependencies():
    text = """from setuptools import setup
setup(
    description="Brotli utility",
    install_requires=read_requirements("brotli-requirements.txt"),
    extras_require={"brotli": ["zlib"]},
)
"""
    assert dependencies.dependency_matches(text, "setup.py") == []


def test_setup_alias_graph_is_bounded_and_handles_annotations_without_values():
    source = 'unused: str\na0 = ["brotli"]\n'
    source += "\n".join(f"a{i} = [a{i - 1}, a{i - 1}]" for i in range(1, 1100))
    source += "\nsetup(install_requires=a1099)\n"
    assert [row["text"] for row in dependencies.dependency_matches(source, "setup.py")] == [
        "brotli"
    ]
    assert (
        dependencies.dependency_matches("a = b\nb = a\nsetup(install_requires=a)", "setup.py") == []
    )


def test_setup_literal_kwargs_and_list_concatenation_are_followed_without_execution():
    source = """from setuptools import setup
extras = ["zlib"]
requirements = ["brotli"] + extras
kwargs = {"description": "Brotli prose", "install_requires": requirements}
setup(**kwargs)
"""
    assert dependencies.dependency_matches(source, "setup.py") == [
        {"field": "install_requires", "text": "brotli", "line": 3}
    ]


def test_poetry_group_names_are_not_dependencies_without_dependency_entries():
    text = """[tool.poetry.group.brotli]
optional = true

[tool.poetry.group.runtime.dependencies]
zlib = "*"
"""
    assert dependencies.dependency_matches(text, "pyproject.toml") == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("name", "parser_module", "text", "kind"),
    [
        ("pipfile", dependencies.tomllib, '[packages]\nzlib="*"', "Pipfile TOML"),
        ("pipfile.lock", dependencies.json, '{"default":{"zlib":{}}}', "Pipfile lock JSON"),
    ],
    ids=["toml-depth-error", "json-depth-error"],
)
def test_recursive_structured_metadata_fails_closed_without_a_brotli_token(
    name, parser_module, text, kind, monkeypatch
):
    def depth_error(_text):
        raise RecursionError

    monkeypatch.setattr(parser_module, "loads", depth_error)
    assert dependencies.dependency_matches(text, name) == [
        {
            "text": (
                f"Incomplete {kind} dependency parsing: nesting exceeds the parser depth; "
                "selection is unresolved."
            ),
            "parse_incomplete": True,
        }
    ]


def test_deep_json_preserves_dependency_when_parser_accepts_it():
    # JSON nesting capacity differs between Python builds. Successful parsing is
    # valid; a decoder that rejects it must still produce incomplete evidence.
    text = '{"default":{"zlib":' + "[" * 50_000 + "0" + "]" * 50_000
    text += ',"brotli":{"version":"==1.2.1"}}}'
    try:
        dependencies.json.loads(text)
    except RecursionError:
        assert dependencies.dependency_matches(text, "pipfile.lock")[0]["parse_incomplete"]
    else:
        rows = dependencies.dependency_matches(text, "pipfile.lock")
        assert [row["field"] for row in rows] == ["default.brotli"]


def test_deep_dotnet_dependency_graph_uses_iterative_traversal():
    payload = "{}"
    for _ in range(2_000):
        payload = '{"zlib":{"dependencies":' + payload + "}}"
    text = '{"dependencies":{"net9.0":' + payload + "}}"
    assert dependencies.dependency_matches(text, "packages.lock.json") == []


def test_each_structured_manifest_parser_retains_only_one_lookahead_row():
    count = dependencies.DEPENDENCY_MATCH_LOOKAHEAD
    cases = {
        "pyproject.toml": "[project]\ndependencies=["
        + ",".join(f'"brotli-{index}"' for index in range(100))
        + "]",
        "setup.py": "setup(install_requires=["
        + ",".join(f'"brotli-{index}"' for index in range(100))
        + "])",
        "setup.cfg": "[options]\ninstall_requires=\n"
        + "\n".join(f"  brotli-{index}" for index in range(100)),
        "pipfile": "[packages]\n" + "\n".join(f'brotli-{index}="*"' for index in range(100)),
        "pipfile.lock": '{"default":{'
        + ",".join(f'"brotli-{index}":{{"version":"*"}}' for index in range(100))
        + "}}",
        "app.csproj": "<Project>"
        + "".join(f'<PackageReference Include="brotli-{index}" />' for index in range(100))
        + "</Project>",
        "packages.lock.json": '{"dependencies":{"net9.0":{'
        + ",".join(f'"brotli-{index}":{{}}' for index in range(100))
        + "}}}",
    }
    for name, text in cases.items():
        assert len(dependencies.dependency_matches(text, name)) == count

name: Checks

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  test:
    name: Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    strategy:
      matrix:
        python-version: ['3.12', '3.13', '3.14', '3.15']
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@07a047e608db84b3d8c06cd9a7c7dcc9c355c18e # v10.3.2
        with:
          version: '0.13.5'
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      - name: Install development tools
        run: uv sync --locked
      - name: Check formatting, lint, and types
        if: matrix.python-version == '3.12'
        run: |
          uv run --locked ruff format --check .
          uv run --locked ruff check .
          uv run --locked ty check skills/brotli-checker/scripts scripts tests
      - name: Run offline tests
        run: uv run --locked pytest

  macos:
    name: Python 3.12 (macOS)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@07a047e608db84b3d8c06cd9a7c7dcc9c355c18e # v10.3.2
        with:
          version: '0.13.5'
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: Run portable offline tests
        run: uv run --locked pytest

  trailmark:
    name: Trailmark source discovery
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@07a047e608db84b3d8c06cd9a7c7dcc9c355c18e # v10.3.2
        with:
          version: '0.13.5'
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: Run real parser integration tests
        env:
          BROTLI_TRAILMARK_TESTS: '1'
        run: uv run --locked pytest tests/test_source_discovery.py --no-cov

  node-fetch:
    name: Built-in Node fetch
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '24.22.1'
          package-manager-cache: false
      - name: Check benign Brotli response decoding
        run: make verify-node-fetch

  mutation:
    name: Mutations (${{ matrix.module }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        module:
          - brotli_binary_data
          - brotli_binary_inventory
          - brotli_binary_match
          - brotli_binary_metadata
          - brotli_binary_triage
          - brotli_dependencies
          - brotli_inventory
          - brotli_source_discovery
          - brotli_source_leads
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@07a047e608db84b3d8c06cd9a7c7dcc9c355c18e # v10.3.2
        with:
          version: '0.13.5'
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: Run module mutation tests
        env:
          MUTATION_MODULE: ${{ matrix.module }}
        run: |
          make known-answers
          uv run --locked --group mutation pytest --gremlins --no-cov --gremlin-executor=subprocess --gremlin-targets="skills/brotli-checker/scripts/${MUTATION_MODULE}.py"
      - name: Retain mutation evidence
        if: success() || failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: scanner-mutation-${{ matrix.module }}
          path: coverage/gremlins/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

  mutation-gate:
    name: Scanner mutation tests
    needs: mutation
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read # Download mutation artifacts from this workflow run.
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Require every shard to finish
        env:
          SHARD_RESULT: ${{ needs.mutation.result }}
        run: test "$SHARD_RESULT" = success
      - name: Download per-module results
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: gh run download "$RUN_ID" --pattern 'scanner-mutation-*' --dir mutation-reports
      - name: Enforce complete aggregate score
        run: python3 scripts/check_mutation_score.py mutation-reports/*/gremlins.json

error-on-warning = true

testpaths = ["tests"]

cache = false
report = ["json", "html"]

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
source = ["skills/brotli-checker/scripts"]

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 80
show_missing = true
exclude_also = ["^if __name__ =="]

[dependency-groups]

    "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
    "ruff>=0.17.2",
    "trailmark==0.7.0",
    "ty>=0.0.91",
]

interface:
  display_name: "Brotli Security Checker"
  short_description: "Check whether your app needs a Brotli security update"

# Brotli Checker

Brotli Checker finds copies of the Brotli decoder that may need an update for
[CVE-2026-111497](skills/brotli-checker/references/advisory.md). Install it as a
Claude Code or Codex skill, then ask it to check your project.

The skill scans source, dependencies, app packages, and unpacked container
filesystems. It checks source fingerprints and supported ELF binary code,
investigates which copies the app uses, and explains what to update or review.
Each copy keeps its own result.

For source review, [Trailmark](https://github.com/trailofbits/trailmark) maps calls
to the decoder and fetch APIs, helping the assistant find callers to inspect.
The scanner finds suspect parts; Trailmark helps show how the code connects.
The assistant checks whether those connections apply to the running app.

## Install and use

Ask Claude Code or Codex:

```text
Install the brotli-checker skill from https://github.com/trailofbits/brotli-checker/tree/main/skills/brotli-checker
```

For manual installation, copy the entire `skills/brotli-checker` folder into
`~/.claude/skills/` ([Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills)) or
`~/.codex/skills/` (Codex). Start a new session, open the project to check, and ask:

```text
Use brotli-checker to check this project and tell me whether I need to update anything.
```

You can also name a folder or app package. With only a website address, the skill
explains what is missing and prepares a request for your hosting provider.
HTTP headers cannot establish the decoder's patch status.

Requires **Python 3.12–3.15** and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for Trailmark
source discovery. The standalone scanner uses only the standard library.

## Run the scanner directly

To collect local evidence without an agent:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/trailofbits/brotli-checker.git
cd brotli-checker
python3 skills/brotli-checker/scripts/brotli_inventory.py /path/to/application
```

The default output explains findings and next steps. Add `--json` for per-copy
evidence, coverage gaps, and a plain-language `user_summary`. See the
[scanner guide](docs/usage.md) for flags, exit codes, Trailmark source discovery,
binary inventory, and disassembly review.

## Understand the result

Affected code calls for an update or vendor-backport review. Version and
dependency findings need confirmation against the app's actual build. A fixed
copy does not clear other bundled copies, and an empty scan does not establish
that an app is safe.

The scanner reads files without executing application code or sending network
probes. Packaged compiled references cover x86, x86-64, ARM/Thumb, AArch64,
RISC-V64, PowerPC64 little-endian, s390x, MIPS32/64 in both byte orders, and
LoongArch64 ELF builds. Coverage depends on compiler and build flags; see the
[build matrix](docs/usage.md#compiled-decoder-evidence). Unsupported formats,
skipped files, and resource limits produce coverage gaps. Finding affected code does not establish that a
running app uses it or that an attacker can reach it.

Rules use an advisory snapshot dated **2026-10-23**. Check current vendor guidance
for updates and backports.

## Documentation

- [Scanner guide](docs/usage.md): commands, output, limits, and binary review.
- [Advisory](skills/brotli-checker/references/advisory.md): fixed versions,
  fingerprints, and provenance.
- [Reachability](skills/brotli-checker/references/reachability.md): investigating
  Node, Electron, Java, fonts, TLS, and compiled code.
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): development setup and checks.
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): release history.
- [Security policy](SECURITY.md): private vulnerability reporting.

[MIT](LICENSE). Compiled Brotli references retain their
[upstream notices](skills/brotli-checker/references/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

    block = hashlib.sha256(salt + name.encode()).digest()
    return (block * ((size + len(block) - 1) // len(block)))[:size]


def relocatable_function_sections(  # noqa: C901 -- One compact ELF fixture builder.
    *,
    salt=b"fixed",
    missing_role=None,
    colocated=False,
    unrelated=20,
    malformed_role=None,
):
    names = [name for role, name in ROLE_NAMES.items() if role != missing_role]
    names.extend(HELPER_NAMES)
    code_specs: list[CodeSpec] = []
    symbols = []
    if colocated:
        contents = _code("complete-text", salt, 768)
        code_specs.append({"content": contents, "names": names})
    else:
        for name in names:
            size = 320 if name == ROLE_NAMES["process"] else 64
            code_specs.append({"content": _code(name, salt, size), "names": [name]})
    code_specs.extend(
        {"content": _code(f"unrelated-{index}", salt, 48), "names": []}
        for index in range(unrelated)
    )

    offset = matcher.ELF_HEADER.size
    payload = bytearray()
    section_rows = [(0,) * 10]
    for spec in code_specs:
        section_index = len(section_rows)
        section_offset = offset + len(payload)
        payload.extend(spec["content"])
        section_type = matcher.SHT_PROGBITS
        section_flags = matcher.SHF_ALLOC | matcher.SHF_EXECINSTR
        if any(name == ROLE_NAMES.get(malformed_role) for name in spec["names"]):
            if malformed_role == "literal":
                section_type = 8  # SHT_NOBITS cannot own file-backed functions.
            elif malformed_role == "command":
                section_flags = matcher.SHF_EXECINSTR
        section_rows.append(
            (
                0,
                section_type,
                section_flags,
                0,
                section_offset,
                len(spec["content"]),
                0,
                0,
                16,
                0,
            )
        )
        stride = max(1, len(spec["content"]) // max(1, len(spec["names"])))
        for symbol_index, name in enumerate(spec["names"]):
            address = symbol_index * stride
            size = min(16, len(spec["content"]) - address)
            if malformed_role == "distance" and name == ROLE_NAMES["distance"]:
                size = len(spec["content"]) + 1
            symbols.append((name, section_index, address, size))

    strings = bytearray(b"\0")
    name_offsets = {}
    for name, _, _, _ in symbols:
        name_offsets[name] = len(strings)
        strings.extend(name.encode() + b"\0")
    string_index = len(section_rows)
    string_offset = offset + len(payload)
    payload.extend(strings)
    section_rows.append((0, matcher.SHT_STRTAB, 0, 0, string_offset, len(strings), 0, 0, 1, 0))

    symbol_struct = struct.Struct("<IBBHQQ")
    symbol_bytes = bytearray(symbol_struct.size)
    for name, section_index, address, size in symbols:
        symbol_bytes.extend(
            symbol_struct.pack(
                name_offsets[name], matcher.STT_FUNC, 0, section_index, address, size
            )
        )
    symbol_offset = offset + len(payload)
    payload.extend(symbol_bytes)
    section_rows.append(
        (
            0,
            matcher.SHT_SYMTAB,
            0,
            0,
            symbol_offset,
            len(symbol_bytes),
            string_index,
            len(symbols) + 1,
            8,
            symbol_struct.size,
        )
    )
    section_offset = offset + len(payload)
    ident = b"\x7fELF\x02\x01\x01" + bytes(9)
    header = matcher.ELF_HEADER.pack(
        ident,
        1,
        matcher.EM_AARCH64,
        1,
        0,
        0,
        section_offset,
        0,
        matcher.ELF_HEADER.size,
        0,
        0,
        matcher.SECTION_HEADER.size,
        len(section_rows),
        0,
    )
    return header + payload + b"".join(matcher.SECTION_HEADER.pack(*row) for row in section_rows)


def linked_elf(payload):
    data_offset = matcher.ELF_HEADER.size + matcher.PROGRAM_HEADER.size
    ident = b"\x7fELF\x02\x01\x01" + bytes(9)
    header = matcher.ELF_HEADER.pack(
        ident,
        2,
        matcher.EM_AARCH64,
        1,
        0,
        matcher.ELF_HEADER.size,
        0,
        0,
        matcher.ELF_HEADER.size,
        matcher.PROGRAM_HEADER.size,
        1,
        0,
        0,
        0,
    )
    program = matcher.PROGRAM_HEADER.pack(
        1, 5, data_offset, 0x400000, 0x400000, len(payload), len(payload), 16
    )
    return header + program + payload

CODE_OFFSET = 0x100
CODE_ADDRESS = 0x400100


def encoded_version(major: int, minor: int, patch: int) -> int:
    return major << 24 | minor << 12 | patch


def x86_return(value: int, *, cet: bool = False, frame: bool = False) -> bytes:
    code = b"\xb8" + value.to_bytes(4, "little") + b"\xc3"
    if frame:
        code = bytes.fromhex("554889e5") + code[:-1] + b"\x5d\xc3"
    if cet:
        code = bytes.fromhex("f30f1efa") + code
    return code


def move_wide(opcode: int, immediate: int, shift: int = 0, register: int = 0) -> int:
    return opcode | (shift // 16 << 21) | (immediate << 5) | register


def aarch64_return(value: int) -> list[int]:
    low = value & 0xFFFF
    high = value >> 16
    words = [move_wide(0x52800000, low)]
    if high:
        words.append(move_wide(0x72800000, high, 16))
    return [*words, 0xD65F03C0]


def words(values: list[int]) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(f"<{len(values)}I", *values)


def elf_with_symbols(  # noqa: PLR0913 -- ELF fixture corruption controls are explicit.
    code: bytes,
    machine: int,
    symbols: list[dict],
    *,
    owner_type: int = 1,
    owner_flags: int = 6,
    owner_address: int = CODE_ADDRESS,
    owner_offset: int = CODE_OFFSET,
    program_flags: int = 5,
    string_type: int = 3,
    symbol_entry_size: int = metadata.SYMBOL.size,
    symbol_table_copies: int = 1,
) -> bytes:
    strings = bytearray(b"\0")
    packed_symbols = [metadata.SYMBOL.pack(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)]
    for symbol in symbols:
        name_offset = symbol.get("name_offset")
        if name_offset is None:
            name_offset = len(strings)
            strings.extend(symbol["name"].encode("ascii") + b"\0")
        packed_symbols.append(
            metadata.SYMBOL.pack(
                name_offset,
                symbol.get("info", 0x12),
                0,
                symbol.get("index", 1),
                symbol.get("address", CODE_ADDRESS),
                symbol.get("size", len(code)),
            )
        )
    symbol_bytes = b"".join(packed_symbols)
    symbol_offset = (CODE_OFFSET + len(code) + 7) & ~7
    string_offset = symbol_offset + len(symbol_bytes)
    section_offset = (string_offset + len(strings) + 7) & ~7
    sections = [
        (0,) * 10,
        (0, owner_type, owner_flags, owner_address, owner_offset, len(code), 0, 0, 4, 0),
        (0, string_type, 0, 0, string_offset, len(strings), 0, 0, 1, 0),
    ]
    sections.extend(
        (0, 2, 0, 0, symbol_offset, len(symbol_bytes), 2, 0, 8, symbol_entry_size)
        for _ in range(symbol_table_copies)
    )
    header = matcher.ELF_HEADER.pack(
        b"\x7fELF\x02\x01\x01" + bytes(9),
        3,
        machine,
        1,
        0,
        matcher.ELF_HEADER.size,
        section_offset,
        0,
        matcher.ELF_HEADER.size,
        matcher.PROGRAM_HEADER.size,
        1,
        matcher.SECTION_HEADER.size,
        len(sections),
        0,
    )
    program = matcher.PROGRAM_HEADER.pack(
        1,
        program_flags,
        CODE_OFFSET,
        CODE_ADDRESS,
        CODE_ADDRESS,
        len(code),
        len(code),
        0x1000,
    )
    result = bytearray(header + program)
    result.extend(bytes(CODE_OFFSET - len(result)))
    result.extend(code)
    result.extend(bytes(symbol_offset - len(result)))
    result.extend(symbol_bytes)
    result.extend(strings)
    result.extend(bytes(section_offset - len(result)))
    result.extend(b"".join(matcher.SECTION_HEADER.pack(*section) for section in sections))
    return bytes(result)

def object_with_relocation(identity, kind, code, offset=128, *, rela=True):
    machine, bits, byteorder = identity
    order = "<" if byteorder == "little" else ">"
    small = bits == 32
    header = struct.Struct(order + ("16sHHIIIIIHHHHHH" if small else "16sHHIQQQIHHHHHH"))
    section = struct.Struct(order + ("IIIIIIIIII" if small else "IIQQQQIIQQ"))
    relocation = struct.Struct(order + (("II" if small else "QQ") + ("i" if small else "q") * rela))
    info = kind
    if machine == 8 and not small:
        info = int.from_bytes(bytes(7) + bytes([kind]), byteorder)
    relocation_bytes = relocation.pack(offset, info, *([0] if rela else []))
    section_offset = header.size + len(code) + relocation.size
    sections = [
        (0,) * 10,
        (0, 1, 6, 0, header.size, len(code), 0, 0, 4, 0),
        (
            0,
            4 if rela else 9,
            0,
            0,
            header.size + len(code),
            relocation.size,
            0,
            1,
            4,
            relocation.size,
        ),
    ]
    ident = b"\x7fELF" + bytes((1 if small else 2, 1 if byteorder == "little" else 2, 1)) + bytes(9)
    return (
        header.pack(
            ident, 1, machine, 1, 0, 0, section_offset, 0, header.size, 0, 0, section.size, 3, 0
        )
        + code
        + relocation_bytes
        + b"".join(section.pack(*row) for row in sections)
    )

def replace_header(data, index, value):
    result = bytearray(data)
    fields = list(matcher.ELF_HEADER.unpack_from(result))

def replace_section(data, index, field, value):

    offset = header[6] + index * matcher.SECTION_HEADER.size
    fields = list(matcher.SECTION_HEADER.unpack_from(result, offset))
    fields[field] = value
    matcher.SECTION_HEADER.pack_into(result, offset, *fields)
    return bytes(result)

def reference(state="fixed", machine=183, salt=b"fixed"):
    code = b"".join(hashlib.sha256(salt + bytes([i])).digest() for i in range(16))
    return {
        "id": state + salt.hex(),

        "machine": machine,

        "source": "test fixture, not a Brotli signature",

def elf(payload, machine=183, *, flags=5, kind=2, prefix=b"", elf_class=64, byteorder="little"):  # noqa: PLR0913 -- Independent ELF fixture controls.
    order = "<" if byteorder == "little" else ">"
    header_struct = struct.Struct(
        order + ("16sHHIQQQIHHHHHH" if elf_class == 64 else "16sHHIIIIIHHHHHH")
    )
    program_struct = struct.Struct(order + ("IIQQQQQQ" if elf_class == 64 else "IIIIIIII"))
    header = header_struct.pack(
        b"\x7fELF"
        + bytes((2 if elf_class == 64 else 1, 1 if byteorder == "little" else 2, 1))
        + bytes(9),
        kind,
        machine,
        1,
        0,
        header_struct.size,
        0,
        0,
        header_struct.size,
        program_struct.size,
        1,
        0,
        0,
        0,
    )
    contents = prefix + payload
    fields = (
        1,
        flags,
        len(header) + program_struct.size,
        0x401000,
        0x401000,
        len(contents),
        len(contents),
        1,
    )
    if elf_class == 32:
        fields = (fields[0], *fields[2:6], fields[6], fields[1], fields[7])
    program = program_struct.pack(*fields)
    return header + program + contents

def relocatable(machine=183, relocation_kind=283):
    code = bytes.fromhex(reference()["code"])
    relocation = matcher.RELOCATION.pack(128, relocation_kind, 0)
    sections = [
        (0,) * 10,
        (0, 1, 6, 0, 64, len(code), 0, 0, 4, 0),
        (0, 4, 0, 0, 64 + len(code), 24, 0, 1, 8, 24),
    ]
    header = matcher.ELF_HEADER.pack(
        b"\x7fELF\x02\x01\x01" + bytes(9),
        1,
        machine,
        1,
        0,
        0,
        64 + len(code) + 24,
        0,
        64,
        0,
        0,
        64,
        len(sections),
        0,
    )
    return header + code + relocation + b"".join(matcher.SECTION_HEADER.pack(*s) for s in sections)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("machine", "kind"), [(62, 1), (62, 2), (62, 4), (183, 283), (183, 275), (183, 277)]
)
def test_reference_generation_preserves_nonrelocation_bits(machine, kind):
    obj = relocatable(machine, kind)
    generated = matcher.reference_from_object(bytes(obj), reference())
    mask = bytes.fromhex(generated["mask"])
    expected = matcher.relocation_mask(machine, kind)
    assert mask[:128] == b"\xff" * 128
    assert mask[128 : 128 + len(expected)] == expected
    assert mask[128 + len(expected) :] == b"\xff" * (512 - 128 - len(expected))
    assert generated["object_sha256"] == hashlib.sha256(obj).hexdigest()


def test_unsupported_object_relocations_and_layouts():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Unsupported executable relocation"):
        matcher.reference_from_object(relocatable(relocation_kind=999), reference())
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="relocatable"):
        matcher.reference_from_object(elf(b"code"), reference())
    obj = bytearray(relocatable())
    section_offset = matcher.elf_header(bytes(obj))[6]
    struct.pack_into("<Q", obj, section_offset + 64 + 8, 0)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="one complete executable section"):
        matcher.reference_from_object(bytes(obj), reference())
    obj = bytearray(relocatable())
    struct.pack_into("<I", obj, section_offset + 128 + 4, 9)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="RELA"):
        matcher.reference_from_object(bytes(obj), reference())
    obj = bytearray(relocatable())
    struct.pack_into("<Q", obj, section_offset + 128 + 32, 23)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Malformed relocation"):
        matcher.reference_from_object(bytes(obj), reference())
